A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KASER research, with matching authors, method, datasets, and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original KASER experiments on CodeWorkout and FalconCode, including comparative results, reward ablations, human annotation evaluation, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports additional prompting-model comparisons, human validation, error-type results, and an all-submissions evaluation.

M1.justification: The knowledge estimator, knowledge-guided SFT, GRPO procedure, three-part reward, and annotation pipeline are unchanged. The retained appendix prompts confirm no documented change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CodeWorkout Java and FalconCode Python student-code prediction tasks. The added analyses stratify errors or broaden submission selection within this setup; they do not document a new dataset, learner population, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated 7B variants of PersonaPrompt and ICL alongside their retained 32B variants on both datasets. ParaStudent, Student SFT, and the per-problem comparator panel remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds 7B prompting configurations, error-type precision/recall/F1 evaluation at K=1 on CodeWorkout, and a human classification check using Jaccard agreement on 50 randomly sampled generated codes. Appendix C additionally evaluates all submissions. Existing main-experiment splits, training settings, and generation procedures are retained; the all-submissions setup receives little detail.

E4.justification: V2 extends human judge validation by error category, adds a separate error-type classification check, and quantifies KASER versus Student SFT performance by error type. Appendix C checks performance beyond first submissions. Existing reward ablations, diversity visualization, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Five-fold averaging, standard deviations, and paired t-tests with p<0.05 remain unchanged. The added agreement scores and supplementary point estimates do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation, repeated-run, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Retained scores in Table 1 and v1 Table 2/v2 Table 3 are unchanged. V2 adds 7B prompting, human-validation, error-type, and all-submissions results; its new Table 5 reports IoU@5 of 0.179 for KASER versus 0.143 for SFT under the all-submissions setting. Appendix A revises FalconCode averages from 16.3 to 20.3 tokens, 15.8 to 5.03 lines, and 2.35 to 1.83 errors per incorrect submission, without establishing a preprocessing change.

T1.justification: The knowledge-state definitions, training objectives, GRPO formulation, and reward Equations 1–3 are retained. No mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: hybrid-reward GRPO aligns simulated errors with student knowledge and improves code/error prediction and problem-level diversity/coverage. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets error-type recall gains as broader error coverage consistent with its reward design and strengthens claims about judge classification reliability. Existing limitations remain. Its new claim of superiority across all error-type metrics overstates Table 2, where precision ties at 1.00.

D1.justification: V2 adds a concrete code-repository link in Section 1.1, whereas v1 only promises a release. The supplied PDFs establish this access-information addition, not repository availability. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Koutcheme et al. (2026) on student-code simulation and Talpaert et al. (2019) and Luo and Duan (2025) for broader RL context. Consolidating duplicate Liu et al. (2022) references and updating Duan bibliography metadata do not change the underlying cited works.

P1.justification: Most wording and narrative structure are retained. Local additions expand validation and results discussion, add acknowledgments and a quantitative Appendix C, and shift the former Appendices C–E to D–F. Bibliographic and wording edits are limited.

P2.justification: V2 adds error-type Table 2 and all-submissions Table 5, expands Table 1 with model-size variants, and renumbers retained tables. Figure 1 receives a small label correction, and pagination and float placement change. The existing figures, code-example displays, and overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens validation through error-category human checks, additional prompting-model controls, and an all-submissions evaluation, while adding useful code-access information. The headline results remain stable. These benefits outweigh limited reporting weaknesses: Appendix C leaves its setup underspecified, and the new all-metrics superiority statement conflicts with tied precision in Table 2.
